title: Two on the Seat
hook: Both cats. First time since the lot.
scene: Ice at night, the Menace still at the same curb. Mya is back. Gracie never left. Orange tabby and brown mackerel on the passenger seat — cream chest, dark stripe — the first time both have been in one frame since the lot. The carrier sits open on the floor next to the seat. The engine is still. This is not a rebuke. It is the next thing you do with a load that cannot buckle itself. The road is ice. They are two moving weights.
decision: Both cats are on the seat and you have not rolled. What do you do with the load?

options.text: Roll now — they have always ridden loose and tonight is not different
options.result: You take the ice with two loose weights. Mya hits the dash. Gracie hits Mya. Your eyes leave the glass. A curb finds the plow. He did not hand her back so you could invent a lap.

options.text: Belt Mya and leave Gracie — one secured is enough
options.result: A cat is not a shape a belt understands. She is out of it before you finish. Gracie is already on the defrost. You spent the curb on a knot and still have two loose.

options.text: Hold them both in your lap so they cannot walk the glass
options.result: Mass in your legs on ice. Two jobs, one pair of feet. The right pedal is a negotiation. The stall you have not left yet already wants a story.

options.text: Clip both in the carrier, stow it, then roll
options.result: You box them. The clip bites. They complain once and become a sound on the floor next to the seat. Two cats, one load, secured. You look at the ice, not at a cream chest. That is what you do next.

debrief: An animal in a moving car is a load. Secure it before you roll. Both cats are in the frame again. Two cats, one carrier, then the ice.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: Secure animals before the vehicle moves; unrestrained pets are a load and a distraction. Lands immediately after the handover.
